segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Nine-Point Circle—also called the Feuerbach or Euler circle—is the circle centered at X five with radius R over two, exactly half the circumradius of triangle A B C.

segments.text: It passes simultaneously through nine classical points: the three side midpoints M a, M b, M c of the medial triangle, the three altitude feet H a, H b, H c of the orthic triangle, and the three Euler midpoints halfway from each vertex to the Orthocenter X four.

segments.text: By Feuerbach's theorem, the nine-point circle is internally tangent to the incircle at the Feuerbach Point X eleven and externally tangent to all three excircles, making X five the bridge between the Euler and Feuerbach lines.
